items.value: AUD/USD vs gold, copper, crude oil (economic, cross-asset)
items.detail: Economic cross-asset pair, spot AUD/USD (not CME futures). Multi-horizon Granger causality at 5-minute and daily frequency: causality both ways, stronger at short horizons, commodity -> exchange rate dominant (ratios up to 5 or 10). In-sample causality measures, not a trading test. Zhang, Dufour, Galbraith (2013), CIRANO 2013s-39 (working paper).
items.quote: (1) Granger causality between commodity prices and exchange rates is visible in both directions; (2) it is stronger at short horizons, and becomes weaker as the horizon increases

items.value: AUD futures vs commodity index futures: no Granger causality (daily)
items.detail: Chan, Tse and Williams (NBER-EASE volume, 2011 chapter c11859): contemporaneous relation only, no lead-lag at daily horizon for AUD, CAD, NZD, ZAR futures. Daily horizon; negative for lead-lag.
items.quote: relation- ships exist contemporaneously, but fail to exhibit Granger-causality in either direction.

items.value: US macro releases (08:30 ET employment etc.): conditional-mean jumps, quick adjustment
items.window: 1992-01 to 1998-12, 5-minute Reuters indicative quotes (DM, euro, pound, yen, CHF vs USD)
items.detail: Absorption: conditional mean adjusts quickly ('effectively amounting to jumps'); variance adjusts gradually. Response coefficients plotted at 0, 5 and 10 minutes after. German releases with uncertain times adjust more gradually, 'perhaps for a few hours' (conjecture). Andersen, Bollerslev, Diebold, Vega (NBER w8959; AER 2003). AUD not covered.
items.quote: We show that conditional mean adjustments of exchange rates to news occur quickly, effectively amounting to “jumps,” in contrast to conditional variance adjustments, which are much more gradual

items.value: US releases (08:30 ET) and FOMC: effect completed within a few minutes (EBS EUR/USD)
items.window: January 1999 to January 2004, EBS one-minute data, euro-dollar and dollar-yen
items.detail: Absorption within a few minutes; returns after the first few minutes orthogonal to the surprise; the expected rate a few minutes after equals that an hour later. Volume stays elevated longer (activity, not mean). Chaboud, Chernenko, Howorka, Iyer, Liu, Wright, FRB IFDP 823 (2004).
items.quote: the surprise component of the announcement produces a movement in the conditional mean that is generally completed within a few minutes, and that is effectively a jump.

items.value: RBA policy announcements: rapid impact within 10 minutes, little after
items.window: Australia 1993-07-30 to 2004-06-02 (79 events); spot AUD/USD intraday
items.detail: Kearns and Manners (RBA RDP 2005-02; IJCB 2006): sharp spike in the 10 minutes after the event, coefficients stable over the following six hours (no drift). RBA met 11 times a year then; 8 a year in 2025-26 (E.28 F11). Fetched via Wayback (rba.gov.au answered 403 to curl).
items.quote: In all 4 countries there is a sharp spike in the impact in the 10 minutes following the event, demonstrating that monetary policy announcements have a rapid impact on the exchange rate. The relative stability of the coefficients over the six hours after the event indicate that the surprise has little additional influence after its immediate impact.
